title: Accounting and Tax Services for Digital Nomads

rows.before: Where a Canadian company sits in the picture, section 125 brings the Ontario combined charge on active business income down to about 12.2% within a $500,000 ceiling, read against profit and never against billings.
rows.after: Where a Canadian company sits in the picture, section 125 brings the Ontario combined charge on active business income down to about 11.2% (12.2% before July 1, 2026) within a $500,000 ceiling, read against profit and never against billings.
rows.note: First R1 change on page; parenthetical added.

rows.before: ">It depends on how much profit genuinely stays behind, which is the same test as for anybody else. The arithmetic is the familiar one. Amounts that stay inside a Canadian corporation meet a combined Ontario charge of something near 12.2% while they sit within the $500,000 active-business ceiling; take the same amounts out to live on and they run up a personal scale whose top is 53.53%.
